title: Field Notes 07: the temperament words you already use
caption:
You've been quoting a 2,000-year-old theory without knowing it.

Sanguine, choleric, phlegmatic, melancholy, 'in a good humour': all of them come from the four humours, and so do the French, Spanish and Italian words for mood. And 'mizaj', from the Arabic for 'mixture', still means mood and temperament in Arabic, Persian, Turkish (mizaç), Urdu and Hindi.

Save this for your next quiz night, and send it to the friend who loves a good word origin.
